Airport security lines: I tried to sneak my dog through airport security in a baby carrier, but the TSA agent saw through the ruse—turns out, the x-ray machine doesn’t just scan for weapons, it scans for suspiciously happy animals.
Endless Zoom meetings: I’ve been in so many Zoom meetings lately, I’m starting to think my boss is just a really convincing animated emoji.
First dates: I told my date I love hiking, and she said, "Me too!" So we went to the park and walked in circles for an hour — I guess we're both into "hiking" in the same way I'm into "I'll just pretend I know how to use a salad fork."
Smart home devices (like a Roomba or Ale: I bought a smart fridge that tells me when my milk's expired — now it just yells at me every time I open the door.
Going to the gym for the first time: I went to the gym for the first time and asked the guy next to me if he was a bro, and he said, "No, I'm just here to bench press my loneliness."
Customer service phone menus: I called customer service and just spent 20 minutes navigating a phone menu that had more options than a buffet at a wedding.
Trying to eat healthy/Dieting: I tried to eat healthier by swapping my soda for water — now I just drink soda and pretend I'm hydrated.
The behavior of cats vs. dogs: Dogs will wait by the door for you to come home, cats will wait by the door for you to accidentally leave something edible on the floor.
Self-checkout machines at the grocery st: I tried to scan a bag of chips at the self-checkout, and the machine asked, “Is this a bulk item?” I said, “No, I just really like chips,” and it charged me extra.
Insomnia and trying to fall asleep: I lie awake at night wondering if my brain is just a stubborn kid who refuses to go to bed until I promise to stay up with it.
Buying things you don't need online: I ordered a set of steak knives online, and when they arrived, I realized I already had steak knives — I just never use them because I only eat salad.
Awkward family gatherings: I asked my uncle why he always brings up his ex at family gatherings, and he said, "It's the only way I can get a real conversation going — everyone else just stares at their phones."
Streaming service algorithms (e.g., Netf: I told my Netflix algorithm I like horror movies, and now it’s recommending me documentaries about haunted houses… and a cooking show hosted by a guy named "The Butcher."
Coffee shop baristas and complicated ord: I asked my barista for a latte with extra foam, and she said, "Sure, but I’ll need a second opinion from the foam.”
Commuting in heavy traffic: I tried to meditate in traffic today, but all I could think was, "Why is this red light taking so long to turn green? Is it even a light or just a metaphor for my life?"
Job interviews: I told my boss I was leaving for a better job, and he said, "You're hired!" Turns out, he thought I was applying for a job at his competing business.
Keeping houseplants alive: I bought a houseplant that came with a care guide — turns out it’s a succulent, so I just need to forget about it and hope it doesn’t die of neglect.
Forgetting passwords: I’ve got a password that’s so complicated, even my dog can’t remember it — and he’s seen me type it 50 times.
High school reunions: I went to my high school reunion and saw my ex-wife there — turns out, she didn't just cheat on me, she also had a full-time job and a college degree.
Assembling flat-pack furniture (e.g., IK: I finally assembled my IKEA bookshelf — it took three hours, but now I’m confident I can build a spaceship.
Tech support/Helping parents with techno: I told my dad he needed to update his software, and he said, "I thought updates were just for cars — you know, the thing that makes them go faster."
Alarm clocks and waking up early: I set my alarm for 6 a.m. to be productive, but clearly, the universe thinks I’m a night owl who’s just really bad at it.
The culture of social media influencers: I followed an influencer who said she only eats healthy, then she posted a video eating a whole cake — I guess "healthy" is just a way to say "I’m going to eat this and then feel guilty about it later."
Cryptocurrencies or \"Tech Bros\": I told my tech bro friend I was investing in cryptocurrency, and he said, "Great choice!" Then he added, "Just don't tell your mom — she still thinks Bitcoin is a type of potato."
Going to the dentist: I told my dentist I was afraid of the drill, and he said, "Don’t worry, I’ll just pretend it’s a little bird nesting in your mouth."
Moving to a new apartment: I moved to a new apartment and realized the only thing that fits in the closet is my insecurity.
Annoying neighbors: I told my neighbor I didn't want to hear his music anymore, and he said, "But it's just classic rock!" I said, "Yeah, and I'm just a classic pain in the neck."
Overpacking for a vacation: I packed so much for my trip, I brought a change of clothes for every possible disaster — and then I forgot my passport.
I downloaded a dating app and swiped right on someone, then immediately panicked thinking I had to commit to a relationship — turns out it was just a salad.
Public transportation/Subways: I took the subway to work today and realized I've been riding the same train since 2012 — the only thing that's changed is the number of people who think they're in a movie.
Wedding planning: I told my fiancé we should get married in a chapel — he said, "But I don't want to be *that* committed."
Autocorrect text message fails: I sent a text saying "I'm stuck in traffic," and autocorrect changed it to "I'm stuck in trigonometry." Now my ex thinks I'm still struggling with math, and my boss thinks I'm avoiding work.
Procrastination: I told my friend I’d stop procrastinating, and now I’m sitting here writing this joke instead of doing my taxes.
Group chats that never stop buzzing: It's like being in a relationship with a phone that's always cheating on you.
The cost of living/Being broke: I used to worry about the cost of living, now I just worry about how many times I can say "I'm fine" before someone believes me.
Getting a bad haircut: I got a bad haircut and now I look like I lost a bet with a hedgehog.
Overly complicated modern fitness trends: I tried that new trend where you do burpees while juggling pineapples — turns out, my abs were just fine with the pineapples.
People who talk at the movie theater: I went to see a horror movie, and the guy behind me whispered the entire plot to his friend — I was halfway through the movie and already knew who the killer was.
Cooking disasters: I tried to make a soufflé, and by the time it collapsed, I had already cried twice, once from the smoke alarm and once from the realization that I'm never getting a divorce.
Small talk about the weather: It’s so hot today, I saw a squirrel wearing a shirt that said “I’m not a nut, I’m a professional.”
Modern fashion trends: I tried to keep up with modern fashion trends until I realized the only thing I was trending was being overdue for a haircut.
Waiting in doctors' offices: I’ve noticed that doctors’ offices have these little magazines — they’re always from 2015, and the only thing more outdated than the articles is the person reading them.
Getting older/Turning 30: I turned 30 and realized I’ve finally reached the age where my parents think I’m responsible — but I’m still too young to get a drink.
Video game culture: I told my kid I’d buy him a video game for his birthday, and now he’s screaming, “No, Dad, I want the *real* version with the plastic sword and the manual that’s 500 pages long!”
Corporate buzzwords (e.g., \"Synergy\"): We all know the corporate buzzword for when you're too scared to say "no" — it's called "synergy."
Dealing with landlords: I told my landlord I needed a new lock — turns out he was just waiting for me to say "security deposit" so he could finally use the key he's had for three years.
Astrological signs/Horoscopes: I checked my horoscope and it said, "Today is a good day for deep conversations... with your therapist."
People who overshare online: I follow someone on Instagram who posts a photo of their breakfast, a photo of their coffee cup, a photo of their dog eating their breakfast, and then a carousel of 12 more photos of their dog’s breakfast — I just want to know where the cat is.
Veganism or extreme dietary restrictions: I tried going vegan for a month, then I realized I wasn't eating meat — I was just eating less of everything else.
Trying to assemble a tent/Camping: I tried to assemble a tent last weekend, and let me tell you, the instructions were written by a confused raccoon who’s never seen a screwdriver.
